**The Last Letter**

I found it tucked between the pages of an old, leather-bound book—yellowed with time, the kind of book that smells like dust and regret. The letter was written in a hand I didn’t recognize, though the script was familiar. My own, perhaps, from a life I’ve long since forgotten.

*Dear Future Me,*

If you’re reading this, I’ve already died. Or maybe I’m just waiting. The doctor said it was terminal, but I didn’t believe him. I was too stubborn, too afraid to accept that the world could end without me. So I kept living, even when the pain was too much to bear.

I don’t know how long I have left. Maybe days. Maybe weeks. But I want you to know something: *I’m sorry.*

I’m sorry for the things I said. The things I did. The things I didn’t do. I’m sorry for the way I treated you, for the way I treated myself. I’m sorry for the love I didn’t give you, for the love I gave too late.

I don’t know if you’ll ever read this. Maybe you’ll throw it away, like I threw away my regrets. Maybe you’ll keep it, like I kept the memories that hurt me most.

But if you do, I hope you know this: *I loved you.* Even when I didn’t say it out loud.

Even when I didn’t mean it.

*Forever yours,*
[Name]

I closed the book, the weight of the words pressing against my chest. The letter was dated 2005, but the handwriting was mine—mine, but not mine. Not the one I was now. Not the one who had moved on.

I wondered if I would ever find the person who wrote it. If they were still alive. If they had ever read it.

And if they had, would they forgive me?

I didn’t know. But I hoped so.

Because sometimes, even in the darkest corners of time, love finds a way to survive.
